Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They provided me with a step by step guide for each thing I had to do before the beginning of my semester. It was very easy to understand, and they even offered help from fellow students regarding important things, such as insurances, where language could have been an obstacle.

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level differed from course to course - some felt more academic while others felt more disciplinary and less academic

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It differed significantly. In the host university, there is a huge focus on refelction comments, which add to unnecessary disciplinary measures that do not contribute to learning in any form. It felt like high school all over again. The content of the comments showed very obviously that it not contribute to a more in-depth engagement with the materials and people were just repeating each other. 
I therefor highly encourage a free format like the one in UCPH or reflection comments like the one provided by the course "peace and conflict studies", where the professor asked relevant opinion-based yet thought provoking questions related to the lecture and the reading material, prompting the student to relfect over the topics.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Japanese Culture
Media and society
Peace and conflict studies
Race and ethnicity in the Mordern World

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Peace and conflict studies: It consisted of a great balance of leactures held by the professor, group discussions for reflection and debate, and post reflection comments that reminds the student of what they learned as well as what they are curious about.

Media and society: It consisted of only lectures and three essays that which due date was distributed over the semester. The lectures were very engaging and interesting. It was a course I very much looked forward to attending - not adding reflection comments as part of the course was very great as they are unnecessary and meaningless.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It is not THAT cheap. - You need to save up if you want to live comforably without worrying about your extra spending.
2. It is a great institution, full of helpful students and staff members. However, do not have too high expectations of the SKP buddy program. It is not like the danish tutor program. They are more shy and less engaging, but they try their best.
3. Learn a little bit of japanese or participate in japanese beginner courses if you are not from the japanese major. It helps a lot in boosting your confidence.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cannot think of any at the moment

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Tackling student life with my desire to be a tourist. The country is so beautiful that you keep wanting to explore, but assignments do fill a lot of the exchange. Remember that you are still a student regardless of the country you reside in. In terms of quantity, you should expect a bigger amount. In terms of difficulty, I would say less - but it depends on the person in question. 
Regardless, remember to plan well and distribute your time well so you can enjoy the most o your experience while being a student on the side.
